FIXED ARTWORK: Keep the camera locked and the full 16:9 composition unchanged. Every existing card, icon, letter, timestamp, connector, arrow and endpoint remains in its original position, shape, scale and orientation for all eight seconds. The blue brain in the circular KNOWLEDGE BASE node is a flat printed icon: preserve its exact outer contour, interior curves and center division. It does not think, breathe, rotate, bounce, redraw, grow or morph. Preserve both robot icons and every document icon as printed artwork. No character animation. Text remains visible, unchanged and readable throughout; no typing or rewritten replies.

ALLOWED ANIMATION: Only change the brightness or pale background tint of the specific existing regions named below, one step at a time, using gentle fades. Do not translate, stretch or redraw any artwork. When a connector is highlighted, illuminate its ENTIRE existing length at once; keep its width, path, bends and endpoints unchanged. 0.0-1.0 seconds: Hold the complete reference still and readable.
1.0-2.0 seconds: Gently increase the pale background tint of the existing question bubble containing "What do you offer?"; then return it to its original tint. Keep its text and geometry fixed.

3.0-4.0 seconds: Keep SERVICES gently tinted. Slightly brighten the entire existing blue connector from the right edge of SERVICES to the upper-left endpoint of the KNOWLEDGE BASE circle simultaneously. No moving element or trail follows it. Briefly lighten only the pale circular BACKGROUND behind the brain; the blue brain artwork and KNOWLEDGE BASE lettering remain identical to the first frame.
4.0-5.0 seconds: Slightly brighten the entire existing right-pointing arrow between KNOWLEDGE BASE and the assistant panel, all at once, without moving or extending it. Return the circle background and the SERVICES connector to their original brightness.

The ENTIRE explanation must be rendered inside the video: graphics, connectors, labels, tracking and outputs. No external website overlay will be added. Preserve the full 16:9 composition and existing readable text from the reference; no cropping, camera cuts, panning or zooming. At 0-1 seconds, establish the supplied complete concept. At 1-6 seconds, perform the demonstration described below. At 6-8 seconds, hold a clear final state so the viewer can read the result. A highlight traces the existing white HISTORY line toward the vertical boundary. The cyan FORECAST segment then draws outward from the same last historical point, and its violet uncertainty band unfolds only on the forecast side. Emphasize the three inventory-planning cards after the forecast appears. Preserve chart axes, dates and existing illustrative values from the first frame; do not introduce accuracy scores, money-saved claims or new numbers. The history/forecast boundary stays fixed and the final forecast plus band remain visible. Preserve the exact reference labels and values; animate emphasis, connectors and highlights rather than inventing or rewriting text. Do not introduce extra objects, malformed letters, fluctuating counts, unsupported claims, confidence percentages, unrelated effects or audio. Every explanatory graphic must remain geometrically and temporally consistent with what it describes. Deliver one complete understandable MP4 scene, not background footage waiting for later graphics.
demos.concept: Extend historical observations into a future demand forecast.
acceptanceChecks: Forecast connects continuously to the final historical point.
Uncertainty band appears only on the forecast portion and follows its line.
Historical data stays unchanged; no fabricated accuracy or claimed business result.
